analytical_question: As of 2026-10-13, America/New_York, should this hypothetical delivery fleet begin a limited operational V2G export trial while preserving charge for daily routes?
general_et_finding: V2G requires bidirectional vehicle and charging capability plus utility-permitted reverse power flow; V2B backup and ordinary managed charging are different uses. Technical capability does not establish broad commercial diffusion or site-specific readiness.
application_finding: An operational export trial must establish compatibility, authorized interconnection, and route-charge protection before dispatching power. Managed charging is the strongest near-term alternative for exploring charging flexibility without grid export.
organization_specific_finding: Hypothetical assumptions: vehicles are available, but utility permission and compatibility remain unconfirmed. The innovator posture supports active preparation, not immediate export; unresolved prerequisites could interrupt the proposed trial.

evidence.claim: DOE distinguishes V2B from V2G and describes bidirectional vehicles paired with capable charging equipment.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Department of Energy, Managed and Bidirectional Charging: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Page undated; supplied packet retrieval date: 2026-10-13.
evidence.notes: Supports technology distinctions, not compatibility of this fleet's equipment; an independently dated historical page version was not established.

evidence.claim: DOE advises checking whether utility interconnection agreements permit reverse power flow and identifies managed charging as addressing vehicle energy needs.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Department of Energy, Managed and Bidirectional Charging: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Page undated; supplied packet retrieval date: 2026-10-13.
evidence.notes: Does not establish local authorization, compensation, savings, or manufacturer warranty coverage.

evidence.claim: The fleet has vehicles, an innovator posture, no utility agreement, and unconfirmed vehicle/charger compatibility.
evidence.notes: Not observations of a real organization or field deployment evidence.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Counter-case: an authorized, compatible installation with protected route reserves and agreed liability could justify a bounded operational export experiment.
The packet does not establish local commercial viability or historical diffusion; no later developments are used to resolve those gaps.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in deferring export under the stated assumptions. Fleet-specific technical readiness, warranty treatment, liability allocation, and economic value remain unknown.
value_opportunity_implication: Preparation can preserve the option to test V2G within 6–12 months without assuming export revenue. Compare prospective incremental value against managed charging before committing to operational export.
risk_governance_implication: Treat utility authorization and documented compatibility as export gates; obtain applicable warranty terms and liability allocation rather than assuming acceptance. Innovator appetite does not remove these prerequisites.
recommendation_management_implication: Defer operational grid export. Immediately request utility and manufacturer confirmation and scope an isolated, non-export proof of concept; any energized testing requires its own safety approval. Pass operating capacity and implementation ownership to the Organizational Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reconsider as a bounded experiment when written utility authorization, documented compatibility, warranty treatment, liability allocation, and route-reserve controls are established.
If route-reserve protection cannot be demonstrated during non-export testing, keep export deferred and prioritize managed charging.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Provide the serving utility and site, exact vehicle/charger configuration, and applicable interconnection authorization.
Provide manufacturer warranty terms, proposed liability allocation, and route-energy requirements; commercial adoption judgment remains withheld without them.
